notes: Box score from the Golden State Warriors' 88–87 home win over the Boston Celtics on Sunday, Nov 22, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, checked line by line against the SI box score and, for Boston, StatMuse. All 88 Golden State points and all 87 Boston points add up from the player lines, and the quarter scores (27–17–25–19 to 20–22–33–12) add up to both totals: Golden State led 44–42 at the half and Boston 75–69 after three (Covers; SI; Field Level Media; Boston Globe). Offensive rebounds (19–15), rebounds (45–41), assists (27–26), points in the paint (34–36), fast-break points (4–8), free throws (8 of 10 to 9 of 12) and both biggest leads (Golden State 10, Boston 11) are from Covers; the SI play-by-play shows Boston's 11-point lead at 73–62 late in the third. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Sunday's games.

Golden State closed the third on a 7–2 run and opened the fourth with a 12–2 burst sparked by two Gui Santos threes to lead 81–79 on Yaxel Lendeborg's floater at 8:13 (SI play-by-play; Boston Globe). Boston went back ahead 86–83 on a Derrick White pull-up at 4:21 (SI play-by-play), then missed its final six shots (Field Level Media). Podziemski scored the Warriors' last five points: a fadeaway at 3:19 for 86–85 and the three at 2:38 (SI play-by-play; Yardbarker). His apparent corner three with 1:07 left was waved off on review as an offensive foul (Boston Globe; AP). Jayson Tatum made 1 of 2 free throws with 55.6 seconds left for 88–87 (Field Level Media; Boston Globe), and after Hugo Gonzalez stole an inbounds pass with 17 seconds left, Tatum missed a contested 16-foot fadeaway at the buzzer with Draymond Green guarding him (AP; Boston Globe; Yardbarker). Tatum scored 23 of his 27 in the first half and passed Bill Russell for 8th on the Celtics' career scoring list (Field Level Media; Boston Globe). Golden State snapped a five-game losing streak and won its seventh straight at home (AP; Field Level Media); Boston has lost four straight, its first such skid since 2020-21 (AP; Boston Globe). Stephen Curry is out with an oblique injury (AP; CBS Sports); Boston rested Paul George (CBS Sports). Green's 9 points were a season high (NBC Sports Bay Area). The Warriors host Sacramento on Wednesday, Nov 25 at 10:00 PM ET; the Celtics play at Washington on Tuesday (Covers; AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Brandin Podziemski's 3-pointer with 2:38 left (SI play-by-play: "Brandin Podziemski makes three point jump shot (Gui Santos assists)"; Field Level Media: "Brandin Podziemski's 3-pointer with 2:38 remaining gave Golden State the lead"; Boston Globe: "A Brandin Podziemski 3-pointer with 2:38 left gave the Warriors an 88-86 lead."). The board's Celtics +1 to Warriors +2 is 85–86 to 88–86; Boston's only later point was Tatum's free throw (SI play-by-play). The sources don't say where on the arc it came from or whether he shot it off the catch, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Golden State Warriors or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Brandin Podziemski's listed 6-foot-4 and 205 pounds with No. 2 (Basketball-Reference; Wikipedia), arms scaled to the 6-foot-5.5 wingspan measured at the 2023 NBA Draft Combine (HoopsMatic). He is drawn in Golden State's home white with the default figure (no look on the look sheet yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
